doc.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Choosing Scott Hamilton over Grover Washington
summary: A Rhode Island friend suggested a Scott Hamilton record; Allen wanted that big sound.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: You grew up in a time where you could have, in your early years as a saxophonist, you could have been listening to Grover Washington and that kind of saxophone, but that didn’t get you, huh?

No it didn’t. Actually when I was first starting to play saxophone, a friend, a saxophone player from Rhode Island where I’m from, suggested I pick up a Scott Hamilton record. So I bought a Scott Hamilton record and I heard the great big sound he had, and I said well that’s what I want to sound like.
That was really it then, huh?
